name: T-Bar Reverse Row
why: Heavy row for your lats.
setup: Chest on the pad, feet flat, arms straight.
form: Shoulders back first, then elbows to your hips.
Hold at the top.
Lower until your arms are straight and shoulder blades spread.
tips: Elbows close: more lats. Elbows wide: more upper back.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → elbows just past your body
tempo: Up 1 s · Hold 1 s · Down 3 s

0.note: Elbow path shifts the work between lats and upper back (coaching practice).

name: Single-arm Cable Lat Pulldown
why: Lats stretched, one arm at a time.
setup: Pulley high. Kneel or sit facing it, arm straight up.
form: Pull your elbow down to your side.
Go back up to the full stretch, hold.
tips: Pull with the elbow, not the hand.
rangeOfMotion: Arm straight up → elbow at your side
tempo: Down 1 s · Up 3 s · Hold 1 s

preferred.why: Top-rated lat isolation: elbow tight to the body, big stretch.

name: Single-arm DB Row
why: Lower lats.
setup: Hand and knee on a bench, back flat.
Dumbbell hangs below your shoulder.
form: Pull your elbow back to your hip, not your chest.
Lower until your shoulder blade spreads forward.
avoid: Turning your body to lift more.
rangeOfMotion: Arm hanging → dumbbell at your hip

name: Straight-arm Cable Pulldown
why: Lats with no biceps help.
setup: Pulley high, bar or rope.
Step back, lean forward a little.
form: Arms almost straight, pull down in an arc to your thighs, squeeze.
tips: A rope lets your hands go past your hips.
rangeOfMotion: Arms up → hands at your thighs
tempo: Down 1 s · Hold 1 s · Up 3 s

name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
why: Heavy pulldown for your back.
setup: Hands a bit wider than your shoulders.
Thighs under the pad, lean back a little.
form: Pull the bar to your upper chest.
Go up until your arms are straight and shoulders rise (stretch).
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight up → bar at your upper chest

preferred.why: Top-rated lat exercise: easy to load and progress.

name: Cable Seated Row
why: Heavy row for your back.
setup: Neutral handle, feet on the plate, knees slightly bent.
form: Row to your lower ribs, squeeze.
Let your arms go straight and shoulder blades spread.
tips: A small forward lean at the stretch is fine.
avoid: Leaning back or throwing it with your lower back.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → handle at your lower ribs
tempo: Pull 1 s · Hold 1 s · Return 3 s

preferred.why: Top-rated row: steady cable tension and a deep stretch at the front.

name: Bent Over Barbell Row
why: Heavy free-weight row for the whole back.
setup: Bar over your mid-foot, hands just outside your knees.
Hips back, back flat, chest over the bar.
form: Pull the bar to your belly button.
Lower until your arms are straight.
tips: Keep your body angle the same every rep.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar at your belly

preferred.why: Heavy multi-joint row you can load the most; strength gains are specific to it.

name: Pendlay Row
why: Strict barbell row from the floor each rep.
setup: Bar on the floor over your mid-foot.
Back flat and close to level with the floor.
form: Pull the bar to your lower chest.
Set it down on the floor, reset, repeat.
tips: Each rep starts from a dead stop, so no bouncing.
avoid: Lifting your chest to help the bar up.
rangeOfMotion: Bar on the floor → bar at your lower chest

name: Deficit Pendlay Row
why: Pendlay row with a longer pull at the bottom.
setup: Stand on a plate or low box, bar on the floor.
Back flat, chest over the bar.
form: Pull the bar to your lower chest.
Lower to the floor and let your shoulders reach down.
tips: Use a lighter weight than your normal Pendlay row.
avoid: Rounding your back at the bottom.
Jerking the bar off the floor.
rangeOfMotion: Bar on the floor, arms long → bar at your lower chest

name: Yates Row
why: Underhand barbell row, more upright, aimed at the lats.
setup: Palms up, hands shoulder-width.
Lean forward about 45°, knees soft.
form: Pull the bar to your belly, elbows close.
Lower until your arms are straight.
tips: Lets you go heavier than a flat-back row.
avoid: Leaning back to lift the bar.
Curling the bar with your arms.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar at your belly

0.note: More upright torso lets you load more (coaching practice).

name: Reverse Grip Bent-Over Row
why: Bent-over row with palms up: more lats.
setup: Palms up, hands shoulder-width.
Hips back, back flat, close to level.
form: Pull the bar to your lower belly, elbows close.
Lower until your arms are straight.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar at your lower belly

name: Straight Bar Bench Mid Row
why: Barbell row standing on a bench for a longer pull.
setup: Bar on the end of a bench, you stand on the bench behind it.
Hands shoulder-width, palms down, back flat.
form: Pull the bar to your belly, squeeze.
Lower all the way down.
avoid: Rounding your back at the bottom.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar at your belly
tempo: Up 1 s · Hold 1 s · Down 3 s

name: Smith Machine Bent Over Row
why: Bent-over row on a fixed bar path.
setup: Bar at knee height, hands just outside your knees.
Hips back, back flat.
form: Pull the bar to your belly.
Lower until your arms are straight.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar at your belly

name: Bent Over Two-Dumbbell Row
why: Both arms at once, free to move.
setup: A dumbbell in each hand, palms facing back.
Hips back, back flat, close to level.
form: Pull both dumbbells to your sides.
Lower until your arms are straight.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → dumbbells at your sides

name: Bent Over Two-Dumbbell Row (Palms In)
aliases: Bent Over Two-Dumbbell Row With Palms In
why: Palms in, elbows close: more lats.
setup: A dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Hips back, back flat.
form: Pull the dumbbells to your hips, elbows close.
Lower until your arms are straight.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → dumbbells at your hips

name: Kroc Row
why: Very heavy one-arm row for many reps.
setup: Free hand on a bench or rack, feet split.
Back flat, a little higher than level.
form: Pull the dumbbell to your hip.
Lower until your arm is fully straight.
tips: Straps help when your grip gives out first.
avoid: Twisting so far your chest faces the side.
rangeOfMotion: Arm hanging → dumbbell at your hip

name: T-Bar Row
aliases: Bent Over Two-Arm Long Bar Row
why: Heavy bent-over row with the bar fixed at one end.
setup: Stand over the bar, V-handle under it by the plates.
Hips back, back flat.
form: Pull the plates to your chest.
Lower until your arms are straight.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → plates at your chest

name: One-Arm Long Bar Row
aliases: Bent Over One-Arm Long Bar Row
why: One-arm row with the bar fixed at one end.
setup: Stand beside the bar, hand just behind the plates.
Free hand on your knee, back flat.
form: Pull the plates to your side.
Lower until your arm is straight.
rangeOfMotion: Arm straight → plates at your side

name: Meadows Row
why: One-arm landmine row with a long stretch.
setup: Stand side-on to the end of the bar, feet split.
Overhand grip on the fat end, free arm on your knee.
form: Pull your elbow up and back.
Lower until your shoulder reaches down.
rangeOfMotion: Arm long → elbow past your body

name: Lying T-Bar Row
why: Chest-supported T-bar row: back works, lower back rests.
setup: Chest at the top of the pad, feet set.
Grip the handles, arms straight.
form: Pull the handles to your chest. Squeeze.
Lower until your arms are straight.
tips: Wide grip: more upper back. Close grip: more lats.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → handles at your chest
tempo: Up 1 s · Hold 1 s · Down 3 s

0.note: Grip width shifts the work (coaching practice).

name: Chest-Supported Machine Row
why: Seated machine row, chest on a pad. Easy to push hard.
setup: Seat so the handles are at chest height.
Chest on the pad, arms straight.
form: Pull the handles to your ribs. Squeeze.
Let your arms go straight and shoulder blades spread.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → handles at your ribs
tempo: Pull 1 s · Hold 1 s · Return 3 s

preferred.why: Top-rated row: hits lats and upper back with no lower-back strain.

name: Leverage Iso Row
why: Plate-loaded row, each arm on its own.
setup: Seat so the handles are at chest height.
Chest on the pad.
form: Pull the handles to your ribs. Squeeze.
Return; don't rest the weight between reps.
tips: Can be done one arm at a time.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → handles at your ribs
tempo: Pull 1 s · Hold 1 s · Return 3 s

name: Leverage High Row
why: Pulls down and back from above: lats and upper back.
setup: Seat so you just reach the handles above you.
Knee pad snug.
form: Pull the handles down to your chest. Squeeze.
Return until your arms are straight.
rangeOfMotion: Arms up and forward → hands at your chest
tempo: Down 1 s · Hold 1 s · Up 3 s

name: Dumbbell Incline Row
why: Chest-supported dumbbell row: back works, lower back rests.
setup: Bench at 30–45°, chest on it.
Dumbbells hang straight down.
form: Pull both dumbbells to your sides, squeeze.
Lower until your arms are straight.
rangeOfMotion: Arms hanging → dumbbells at your sides
tempo: Up 1 s · Hold 1 s · Down 3 s

name: Incline Bench Pull
why: Chest-supported row with elbows wide: upper back.
setup: Bench at about 30°, chest on it.
Dumbbells hang, palms facing back.
form: Pull your elbows out and up until level with your back, squeeze.
Lower until your arms are straight.
rangeOfMotion: Arms hanging → elbows level with your back
tempo: Up 1 s · Hold 1 s · Down 3 s

name: Barbell Seal Row
why: Barbell row lying on a high bench: no lower back.
setup: Lie face down on a high bench, bar under it.
Hands a bit wider than your shoulders.
form: Pull the bar up to the bench, hold.
Lower until your arms are straight.
tips: A curved bar lets you pull higher.
avoid: Lifting your chest off the bench.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar at the bench
tempo: Up 1 s · Hold 1 s · Down 3 s

name: Seated One-Arm Cable Row
why: One-arm cable row with room to stretch.
setup: Single handle, feet on the plate.
Sit tall, arm straight.
form: Pull your elbow back to your hip, squeeze.
Let your shoulder reach forward at the end.
rangeOfMotion: Arm straight, shoulder forward → handle at your hip
tempo: Pull 1 s · Hold 1 s · Return 3 s

name: Wide-Grip Cable Row
why: Cable row with hands wide and elbows out: upper back.
setup: Long bar, hands wide, feet on the plate.
Sit tall, arms straight.
form: Pull the bar to your upper belly, elbows out, squeeze.
Return until your shoulder blades spread.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar at your upper belly
tempo: Pull 1 s · Hold 1 s · Return 3 s

name: Inverted Row with Straps
why: Bodyweight row on straps.
setup: Hold the straps, lean back, body straight.
Walk your feet forward to make it harder.
form: Pull your chest to your hands, squeeze.
Lower until your arms are straight.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → hands at your chest
tempo: Up 1 s · Hold 1 s · Down 3 s

name: Pull-Up
why: Bodyweight pull for your back.
setup: Hands a bit wider than your shoulders, palms forward.
Hang with arms straight.
form: Pull up until your chin is over the bar.
Lower until your arms are straight.
tips: Add weight with a belt once you get your reps.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → chin over the bar

preferred.why: Heavy vertical pull, loaded with a belt; strength gains are specific to it.

name: Chin-Up
why: Palms-up pull-up: back plus a lot of biceps.
setup: Palms facing you, hands shoulder-width.
Hang with arms straight.
form: Pull up until your chin is over the bar.
Lower until your arms are straight.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → chin over the bar

name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
why: Palms-in pull-up: easy on the shoulders.
setup: Parallel handles or a V-handle, palms facing each other.
Hang with arms straight.
form: Pull up until your chin is over the bar.
Lower until your arms are straight.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → chin over the bar

name: Close-Grip Front Lat Pulldown
why: Pulldown with hands close, palms forward.
setup: Hands about shoulder-width, palms forward.
Thighs under the pad.
form: Pull the bar to your upper chest.
Go up until your arms are straight.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight up → bar at your upper chest

name: Neutral-Grip Lat Pulldown
why: Palms-in pulldown, elbows close: lats.
setup: V-handle or neutral bar, palms facing each other.
Thighs under the pad.
form: Pull your hands to your upper chest, elbows down to your sides.
Go up until your arms are straight.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight up → hands at your upper chest

name: Underhand Cable Pulldown
why: Palms-up pulldown: lats plus biceps.
setup: Palms facing you, hands shoulder-width.
Thighs under the pad.
form: Pull the bar to your upper chest.
Go up until your arms are straight.
avoid: Curling the bar instead of pulling with your back.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight up → bar at your upper chest

name: Full Range-Of-Motion Lat Pulldown
why: Two high cables, arms crossed: a longer pull than a bar.
setup: Sit or kneel between two high pulleys.
Take each handle with the opposite hand.
form: Pull down in an arc to your shoulders, turning palms to face each other.
Go up to the full stretch.
rangeOfMotion: Arms crossed overhead → hands at your shoulders

name: Cable Incline Pushdown
why: Straight-arm pulldown lying on an incline: lats only.
setup: Incline bench facing away from a high pulley.
Bar overhead, arms almost straight.
form: Pull the bar in an arc down to your thighs.
Go back overhead.
rangeOfMotion: Arms overhead → bar at your thighs

name: Cross-Body Lat Pull-Around
why: One-arm straight-arm pull from across the body: lats stretched.
setup: Pulley high. Kneel or stand side-on, far hand on the handle.
Arm reaching up and across.
form: Sweep your arm down and around to your hip.
Return to the stretch.
rangeOfMotion: Arm up and across → hand at your hip

name: Bent-Arm Barbell Pullover
why: Lats stretched with the arms overhead.
setup: Lie on a flat bench, head at the end.
Bar over your chest, elbows bent.
form: Lower the bar behind your head, elbows staying bent.
Pull it back over your chest.
tips: Go only as far back as your shoulders allow.
avoid: Straightening your elbows as you lower.
rangeOfMotion: Bar over your chest → bar behind your head

name: Inverted Row
why: Bodyweight row under a bar.
setup: Bar in a rack or Smith at waist height.
Hang under it, body straight, heels down.
form: Pull your chest to the bar, squeeze.
Lower until your arms are straight.
tips: Lower bar or feet on a bench: harder.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → chest at the bar
tempo: Up 1 s · Hold 1 s · Down 3 s

name: Shotgun Row
why: Standing one-arm cable row, palm turning up.
setup: Single handle, low pulley.
Step back into a wide split stance, arm straight.
form: Pull your elbow back to your side, palm turning up, squeeze.
Let your shoulder reach forward at the end.
rangeOfMotion: Arm straight, shoulder forward → handle at your side
tempo: Pull 1 s · Hold 1 s · Return 3 s

name: Kneeling High Pulley Row
why: Rope pulled down to your upper chest, elbows out: upper back.
setup: Rope on a high pulley.
Kneel a couple of feet back, arms up in front.
form: Pull the rope to your upper chest, elbows wide, squeeze.
Return until your arms are straight.
rangeOfMotion: Arms up in front → rope at your upper chest
tempo: Pull 1 s · Hold 1 s · Return 3 s

name: One-Arm Kettlebell Row
why: One-arm row with a kettlebell.
setup: Kettlebell in front of your feet.
Hips back, back flat, free hand on your knee.
form: Pull the kettlebell to your hip.
Lower until your arm is straight.
rangeOfMotion: Arm hanging → kettlebell at your hip

name: Two-Arm Kettlebell Row
why: Bent-over row with two kettlebells.
setup: A kettlebell in each hand.
Hips back, back flat, knees soft.
form: Pull both kettlebells to your belly.
Lower until your arms are straight.
tips: Can be done one arm at a time, holding the other still.
rangeOfMotion: Arms hanging → kettlebells at your belly

name: Renegade Row
why: Row from a push-up position: back plus core.
setup: Push-up position, hands on two dumbbells.
Feet wide for balance.
form: Row one dumbbell to your side, then the other.
Keep your hips square to the floor.
tips: Balance limits the weight: a supported row builds more back.
rangeOfMotion: Arm straight → dumbbell at your side

0.note: Ranked low for back growth by coaches (Nippard back ranking).

name: Helms Row
why: Dumbbell row with only your chest on a bench: strict and supported.
setup: Stand behind an incline bench, chest on its top end.
Hips back, torso near level, dumbbells hanging.
form: Pull both dumbbells up and back. Squeeze.
Lower until your arms are straight.
avoid: Lifting your chest off the bench.
rangeOfMotion: Arms hanging → dumbbells at your sides
tempo: Up 1 s · Hold 1 s · Down 3 s

name: Lat Prayer
why: Straight-arm pull from overhead to your hips: lats only.
setup: Rope or bar on a high pulley.
Stand facing it, step back, bend forward about 90°, arms long overhead.
form: Pull your hands down to your hips in an arc, arms almost straight.
Lift your chest a little as they reach your hips, squeeze.
Return to the stretch.
rangeOfMotion: Arms overhead, bent 90° → hands at your hips

name: Machine Lat Pulldown
why: Plate-loaded pulldown, each arm on its own path.
setup: Seat so you just reach the handles, thighs under the pad.
form: Pull the handles down to your shoulders.
Go up until your arms are straight.
tips: Can be done one arm at a time.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight up → hands at your shoulders

name: Machine Pullover
why: Lats only, from a full stretch overhead.
setup: Seat so your shoulders line up with the pivot.
Elbows on the pads, arms overhead.
form: Push the pads down with your elbows until the bar is at your stomach.
Go back up to the stretch.
rangeOfMotion: Arms overhead → bar at your stomach

name: Iso-Lateral Low Row
why: Plate-loaded row from a low angle, each arm on its own.
setup: Chest on the pad, seat so the handles are low, below your chest.
Arms straight, palms down.
form: Pull the handles back and low, toward your hips. Squeeze.
Return until your arms are straight.
tips: Can be done one arm at a time.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → handles at your sides
tempo: Pull 1 s · Hold 1 s · Return 3 s

name: Iso-Lateral D.Y. Row
why: Plate-loaded underhand row that arcs to your hips: lats and mid-back.
setup: Chest on the pad, palms up on the handles.
Arms straight in front.
form: Pull the handles back in an arc toward your hips, squeeze.
Return until your arms are straight.
tips: Can be done one arm at a time.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → handles at your hips
tempo: Pull 1 s · Hold 1 s · Return 3 s

name: Single-Arm Chest-Supported DB Row
why: One-arm row with your chest on a bench: no lower-back strain, no twisting.
setup: Bench at 30–45°, chest on it.
One dumbbell hanging straight down.
form: Pull the dumbbell to your side. Squeeze.
Lower until your arm is straight.
avoid: Turning your body to lift more.
rangeOfMotion: Arm hanging → dumbbell at your side
tempo: Up 1 s · Hold 1 s · Down 3 s

name: Gorilla Row
why: Two kettlebells, rowing one at a time from a deep hinge.
setup: Kettlebells between your feet, wide stance.
Hips back, back flat, a handle in each hand.
form: Row one kettlebell to your hip while pushing the other into the floor.
Lower it, then row the other side.
rangeOfMotion: Arm hanging → kettlebell at your hip

name: Lying Cable Pullover
why: Pullover on a bench with a cable: lats loaded at full stretch.
setup: Bar on a low pulley. Flat bench 2–3 ft away.
Lie with your head toward the pulley, arms overhead.
form: Arms almost straight, pull the bar over you to your waist.
Return until your arms are past your head.
rangeOfMotion: Arms past your head → bar at your waist

name: Single-Arm Straight-Arm Pulldown
why: Straight-arm pulldown one side at a time: lats only, more range.
setup: Handle on a high pulley.
Step back, lean forward a little, arm reaching up.
form: Arm almost straight, pull down in an arc to your thigh.
rangeOfMotion: Arm up → hand at your thigh

name: Kneeling Lat Pulldown
why: Pulldown kneeling at a cable: no seat or knee pad needed.
setup: Bar on a high pulley. Kneel facing it.
Hands about shoulder-width, arms straight up.
form: Pull the bar to your upper chest.
Go up until your arms are straight.
avoid: Sitting back on your heels to pull.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight up → bar at your upper chest

name: Bent-Arm Dumbbell Pullover
why: Lats stretched with the arms overhead, one dumbbell.
setup: Shoulders across a flat bench, hips low, feet flat.
One dumbbell in both hands over your chest, elbows bent.
form: Lower it in an arc behind your head.
Pull it back over your chest.
tips: Go only as far back as your shoulders allow.
avoid: Straightening your elbows as you lower.
rangeOfMotion: Dumbbell over your chest → behind your head

name: Straight-Arm Dumbbell Pullover
why: Lats stretched with the arms overhead, one dumbbell.
setup: Shoulders across a flat bench, hips low, feet flat.
One dumbbell in both hands over your chest, arms straight.
form: Lower it in an arc behind your head.
Pull it back over your chest.
tips: Go only as far back as your shoulders allow.
avoid: Bending your elbows to cheat it back up.
rangeOfMotion: Dumbbell over your chest → behind your head
